summary: This is Agricola stripped down to its friendliest form: no vegetables, no stone, no card-driven asymmetry, just a tight loop of grabbing resources, building rooms, plowing and sowing fields, and fencing pastures to feed your growing family each harvest. It plays fast and teaches worker placement and resource-conversion planning without the brutal food-crisis punishment or the overwhelming card deck of the full game.
praised: Excellent, gentle on-ramp to worker placement and engine-building for newer or younger players
Fixed round-by-round action reveal removes the deckbuilding/drafting complexity of the original
Still delivers real tension over feeding your family and satisfying puzzle-like farm optimization
criticised: Feels thin and less replayable for veteran Agricola players once the novelty wears off
Removing the occupation/minor improvement cards strips out much of the variety and strategic depth fans love
Some feel it's a stepping stone game you outgrow quickly rather than a destination in its own right

interaction.kind: worker placement blocking and action-space denial

scoring.why: Points come from a spread of farm categories (fields, pastures, animals, house size/type, family size) so the winner is whoever balances growth across categories rather than maxing one

similar: Agricola: All Creatures Big and Small
